title: Kaivalya — when purity of mind equals purity of self (3.55–3.56)
hook: the book of powers ends not with a power but with a cleaned window: when the mind is as pure as the seer, there is freedom
tomorrow: The powers by birth, herbs, mantra, discipline, samadhi

segments.voice: Yesterday: taraka, and your line, the instant. Only one instant is real at a time. Did a heavy day get lighter when you shrank it to now? Day four hundred seventy-nine.

Somewhere there's a sliding glass door so clean that people walk straight into it. You've seen it, maybe done it. The glass is still there. It still has a job, holding the weather out. But it's so clear that it no longer adds anything of its own to the garden on the other side. No smudge, no tint, no reflection of the room. You look through it and see only what's there. Book three has spent fifteen days on powers. Here is its last sutra, and it isn't a power at all. It's that door.
screen: `A GLASS DOOR SO CLEAN.` → `PEOPLE WALK INTO IT.` → `IT ADDS NOTHING OF ITS OWN.`

segments.voice: The last sutra of book three: when the purity of the mind's clearest part equals the purity of the seer, kaivalya. The mind's clearest part is sattva, the quality of light and clarity. The seer is purusha, pure awareness, which never needed cleaning. So the work has all been on one side. The glass, not the garden. Practice, discernment, letting go, all of it wipes the glass until it adds nothing of its own. And then the two are equal. Kaivalya comes from kevala, alone, only, whole. Not loneliness. More like standing on its own, needing nothing. The seer, no longer tangled with what it sees. Then the classical commentary adds a line that's easy to miss and hard to forget. This freedom comes whether or not someone has the powers. Fifteen days of invisibility, elephants, gods at the door, and the commentary quietly says: none of that was required. A plain person with a clear mind arrives at the same place. Now look back over book three. Concentration, meditation, absorption. Prajna, samyama. The transformations of the mind. Then the powers, one after another: past and future, other minds, strength, the stars, the heart. The warning in the middle. The elements, the senses, omniscience let go, the gods refused, the instant seen clearly. And at the end, not a greater power, but a cleaner window. Two purities, equal. Tomorrow, the fourth and last book, on freedom itself.
screen: `SATTVA: THE MIND'S CLEAREST PART.` · `ALL THE WORK IS ON THE GLASS.` · `KEVALA: ALONE, WHOLE.` · `WITH OR WITHOUT THE POWERS.` · `BOOK THREE, FROM THE TOP.` · then, large: `EQUAL.`

segments.voice: Today's practice wipes the glass a little. Sit steady and easy, and rest on the breath. Notice whatever the mind is adding right now: a mood, a commentary, a judgment about how this is going. Don't fight it. Just see it as a smudge on the glass, and let it fade on its own. Then look through again at the breath, plain and clear, as it is. Again and again, smudge, seen, clear. The bell holds the time.
Kaivalya. Aloneness, wholeness, freedom: when the mind's clarity is equal to the seer's purity.
Your line: equal. Today, catch one moment where your mood is tinting everything, and wipe the glass: see the person or the task without the tint, just once. Day four hundred seventy-nine.

screen: `DAY 479 COUNTS.` → `BOOK THREE OF THE YOGA SUTRAS, DONE.` → `TOMORROW: THE POWERS BY BIRTH, HERBS, MANTRA.`

howItsDone: In the Yoga tradition, kaivalya is the goal of practice: the seer standing free of entanglement with nature, reached through discernment and dispassion, and teachers stress that it does not depend on gaining any powers.

fork.setup: you've practiced for years with no visions, no powers, nothing dramatic. can you reach kaivalya?
options: no: the powers are the proof.
yes: the commentary says it comes with or without the powers.
only if you reach omniscience first.
fork.reveal: the commentary on the last sutra of book three says freedom comes whether or not one has the powers. what matters is the mind's purity equaling the seer's.

original.note: Sanskrit kaivalya: from kevala (alone, only, whole); aloneness, the freedom of the seer.

trapdoor: what you thought: kaivalya means isolation from the world.
what it means: when the mind's clarity equals the seer's purity, the seer stands free, whole, needing nothing.
what a scholar hears: sattva-purushayoh shuddhi-samye kaivalyam (the last sutra of book three, numbered 3.55 or 3.56); the Bhashya says it comes to one with powers or without.
